utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. Good morning, Madam Registrar. Could you call the case, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. This is case number IT-03-68-T, the Prosecutor versus Naser Oric.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you, Madam. Mr. Oric, can you follow the proceedings in your mother tongue?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Your Honours. Yes. I can follow the proceedings in my own mother tongue.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. I thank you. You may sit down. Good morning to you. Appearances for the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honour. I'm Patricia Sellers for the Office of the Prosecutor. With me are co-counsels, Mr. Gramsci di Fazio, Ms. Joanne Richardson and our case manager, Ms. Donnica Henry-Frijlink. Good morning to the Defence and special welcome back to Judge Eser.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you and what about Mr. Wubben? When are we to expect him back?

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Your Honour, Mr. Wubben is physically back on the premises Office of the Prosecutor but still, related to his illness, he will not be able to be in court today.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Please extend to him our best regards and tell him that we look forward to seeing him back in the courtroom as soon as possible.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Certainly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. Appearances for Naser Oric.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Your Honours. Good morning to the colleagues from the Prosecution. I'm Vasvija Vidovic and, together with Mr. John Jones, I represent Mr. Oric. We are joined by our legal assistant, Ms. Adisa Mehic and our case manager, Mr. Geoff Roberts.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you, Madam Vidovic, and good morning to you and your team. Now, do you have any preliminaries?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, just one point. We received the timetable for the hearings in the upcoming period and allow me to say here that we are extremely interested in speeding things up and managing to finalise things as soon as possible and we've carefully looked into the possibility of still having hearings in the first week of October, even in the absence of one of the Judges. Already last week we found ourselves in a situation which the Trial Chamber listened to the testimonies from two witnesses in this sort of situation. So we wanted to have two quite important witnesses in that period of time, and let me voice our view here. We don't think it would be in the interests of justice this time to listen to those particular witnesses if not all Judges are present. Perhaps it would after all not be better to have a hearing on those days because we would once again then have witnesses here and not all the judges would be present.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. Madam Vidovic, we'll take into consideration your position on this and we need to discuss -- we'll see whether there can be any -- what the possibilities are because I can't tell you here as from now what the position will necessarily be, but those days were needed for serious matters, not -- anyway, we'll see to that. Judge Eser, as you see, is back with us and we expect to have him here throughout the rest of the week saving complications, in which case he has got my authority to leave without even informing me. So that is the position. And then we decide whether to continue with two or whether to continue -- or not to continue at all. But that's the position. Please understand that at the moment we are facing some problems that need to be attended to, and -- they have to be attended to, in other words. And stopping the sittings, according to me, should be the last option. We'll try to explore other possibilities before we come to that. That's number one. Number two, I have informed by Mr. Pitman that he is -- he was trying or he is still trying with the Registry to move next week's afternoon sittings to the morning. That is fine with us and I hope it is fine also with the parties, with the exception of Monday. Monday, because one of the judges would be travelling back to The Hague and I want to make sure that he will be here by the time we start the sitting, we prefer to sit in the afternoon. All right? Thanks. So that sorts out this area. The other thing is this: That we have received a copy of the Defence response to the confidential motion pursuant -- filed pursuant to Rule 70. To be honest with you after first reading of it, I think it does require some time on your part. It's a little bit more complicated than I thought.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Excuse me, Your Honour, might I just ask for -- in terms of clarification of the record, was that the Defence response or was it the Prosecution response.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Prosecution response.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And I think you would require sometime to consult with the government in question as to what the situation is likely going to be like. So we are not going to impose any time limit for you to reply. Feeling certain that as soon as you have a confirmation from that particular government, you will come back to us et cetera, but please do update us on a regular basis, at least once a week, until you get a response from the government.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. May I take it from that that you give us leave to file a reply.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, it's obvious. I mean the kind of response -- I mean, we would need to know what the position is on your part following the Prosecution response before we can hand down a decision. I mean --

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Yes, thank you. It's just so we don't formally seek leave for filing a reply.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: No, you don't need -- take it for granted. The other thing is with regard to Rule 92 bis, first witness, in other words Avdo Huseinovic, when are we expected to have the response.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Your Honour, that will be filed today.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: That's great. With regard to the other two witnesses that -- you had given an indication you would seek to tender their evidence under Rule 92 bis, that is Han Ulens and Rene Caravielhe, I would suggest that we don't waste more time, that you file the relative motion at your earliest so that we handle it. At least I get an indication from the Prosecution -- we'll get an indication from the Prosecution whether they are going to oppose or not, and we will know where we stand. Of course, time will catch up with us very quickly before you even know it. So I would suggest that you file the relative motions as soon as possible.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Yes. In fact, one reason for delay is there is a certain -- potential problems arising with your organisation in question which I won't mention in open court. But that's one of the reasons why there has been some delay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: But what I mean, Mr. Jones, is that I don't know exactly who but I would imagine I can attribute it to -- Mr. Wubben, way back in August, had given an indication that there would probably not be an opposition from the Prosecution as regards these two witnesses so at least it would help the situation to crystallise. You would know exactly whether there is going to be an opposition. The same applies to us. And then you can make your own arrangements how to do it and --

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: It's just that we are waiting a certain authorisation, as it were, before filing from the organisation in question. But we can still file it conditionally, as it were, and then if in the end negotiations don't work out, then we would withdraw one or two of those witnesses.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. Okay. I don't have any -- okay. I don't have any further matters to raise so I think we can bring the witness in. He doesn't enjoy any protective measures?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And I ask you how long -- who is going to take this witness? Madam Vidovic?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I myself, Your Honour. And I will need at least four to four and a half hours. We had provided for three days for these two witnesses, and then for the cross-examination to take about three and a half hours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: The next witness -- will you have him available to start testimony on Thursday? You will.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: That one is still envisaged to take longer than this one.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And you're prepared to make sure that he is kept here over the weekend because it's not likely then that we will finish with his testimony by Friday.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour. That's what the witness expects.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. Why I'm saying that is so that you make it clear to him. Yes. Mr. Tiro, good morning to you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I'm speaking in English and you should be receiving interpretation in a language that you understand. Before I proceed any further, I want to make sure that this is so. In other words, that you are receiving interpretation loud and clear.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [No audible response]

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreters didn't hear the witness. Apparently he said yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. I heard him say yes. If at any time you're not receiving interpretation in a language that you understand, or if there is any problem with the sound level, please draw our attention straight away and we will rectify it, rectify the matter.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So welcome once more. We are about to start with your evidence. You have been summoned here as a Defence witness in this trial, which the Prosecution has instituted against Naser Oric. Our rules require that before you start giving evidence, you make a solemn declaration, which is something identical to an oath in many jurisdictions. The substance or the essence of this solemn declaration is that in the course of your testimony, you will be testifying, you will be speaking the truth, the whole truth and nothing but the truth. The text of the solemn declaration is contained in a piece of paper that Madam Usher standing at your left will now be giving you. Please read it out aloud and that will be your solemn undertaking with us.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: You may sit down. Please make yourself comfortable. And let me explain to you the few remaining things. Madam Vidovic will soon start with her examination-in-chief. That means a series of questions that will not finish today. We will continue with her examination-in-chief tomorrow. After that, Ms. Sellers will be taking you up for cross-examination, and that will take your evidence into Wednesday probably. So try to keep your questions as concise but as precise as possible because that will ensure that you are out of here by the end of our sitting on Wednesday. Otherwise, you will stay here until we finish with you. When I say try to keep your answers as concise and precise as possible, my message to you is to try and answer all questions that are put to you, irrespective of who is putting them to you, in a truthful manner but please try to answer the question, the whole question, and nothing but the question. If you try to give us more information than you are being asked to give, that means you are going to stay here for longer, for a longer period of time. I hope I have made myself understood. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And that you will cooperate to the best of your ability so that you are out of this courtroom by not later than Wednesday.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: The last thing I want to tell you is that between the sittings, and even between breaks but between sittings, that is between today and tomorrow and between tomorrow and the day after, you are not allowed to communicate with anyone on the matters related to your evidence here.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: You can of course contact your family, you can contact friends, you can contact anyone that you like, but not in relation to the matters that you are giving evidence upon or in relation to this trial.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: My name is Carmel Agius, and I am the Presiding Judge. I come from the Mediterranean island of Malta. To my right I have Judge Brydensholt from the Kingdom of Denmark, and to my left I have Judge Professor Albin Eser from Germany.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Tiro.

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: Good morning, Madam.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Since we both speak the same language, I would like to appeal to you to take account of the fact that the interpreters need to finish their sentences after I've asked you a question because some other people in this courtroom don't understand our language. Do you understand that?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: Yes, of course.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Tiro, can you tell the Trial Chamber your full name and surname?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: Hamed Tiro.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: You were born on the 15th of May 1961 in Zapolje?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: In Zapolje.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Is it a hamlet, Gornja Orlica?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: And your father's name is Alija?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Your mother's name is Rasida?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Her maiden name is Memic?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: You have two brothers, they are called Mehmed and Hamdija?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: And you have three sisters?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Nedziba, Zlatka, and Habiba?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: You finished primary school in Bjelovac in 1976?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: In 1978, you finished a builder's trade in Belgrade?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: You did your military service in 1980 in Pljevlja?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Tiro, could you just allow for me to finish my question before you answer and also, on top of that, we would need a short break between my question and your answer.

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: Clear.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: So you did your military service in 1980 in Pljevlje in Montenegro and you were in mountain infantry?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Then you got a job as a builder in Majdanpek in Serbia in 1983?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Between 1983 -- sorry, between 1988 until the war, you had your own private enterprise, as a builder, and you worked at various construction sites?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: And prior to the war, you worked together with both Serbs and Muslims, isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: I would now like to ask the usher to show the witness a map of the area of Srebrenica. It's the same map we've used before but we would like for this witness to take a look at the map and mark a certain number of places that I'm going to ask him about, because we'll ask for this map to be attributed an exhibit number as an exhibit for the Defence. Mr. Tiro, could you please take a look at the map. It is placed on the device that is on your right. Can you take a look at it?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: 727? So this map will become D727, Madam Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Tiro, you said you were born in Zapolje, actually in a hamlet called Gornja Orlica. I would like to ask you to show the Trial Chamber where this hamlet is, where actually Zapolje and Orlica?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. Madam Usher, for the time being he's going to show us. If he's going to mark it give him a red marker, please, because I take it -- I imagine from what I have read so far in the summary that he will be showing us where various positions, military --

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So I keep the colours separate.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. So can you encircle, please put a circle around this spot where you were born? Yes. So, for the record, the witness has encircled the area on the map D727 which contains the two names, Zapolje and Gornji Orlica.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Tiro, before the war, did Muslim population live there?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: 100 per cent.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can you show the Trial Chamber the Serb part of Orlica and then a place called Grabovacka Rijeka?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: [Witness points]

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Could you tell the Trial Chamber how far your hamlet is from Grabovacka Rijeka?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: They are very close.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: And from your hamlet, well, how far is Srpska Orlica?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: 500 metres.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: These hamlets, Grabovacka Rijeka and Srpska Orlica, are they part of some municipality?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: Yes, they are.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Which one?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: Fakovici.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: For the record, the witness has also put a circle around -- is that Stari or Orlica or what? What would be the two letters, ST, in front of Orlica? What do they stand for?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Tiro, the Presiding Judge is asking you about this part that you've called Serb Orlica. Is it called Serb Orlica or Stara Orlica?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: Srpska Orlica.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Just for the sake of clarifying things in the transcript, I asked you what local commune or community are these hamlets a part of? What I mean are Grabovacka Rijeka and Srpska Orlica?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: Srpska Orlica is within the local community of Bjelovac.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: And what about Grabovacka Rijeka?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: Fakovici.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: So we are talking about a local commune, not actually a municipality?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. In Orlica -- now, can you tell us what the ethnic makeup of the population was in Orlica. Apart from the part where you lived, you've already told us that it was Muslim.

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: In Srpska Orlica there were 100 per cent Serbs.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Had there been any Roma in that area?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: The Roma lived in another village which was the Roma village and they were the majority there in that particular village.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: What was the part of the village where they lived?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: Donja Orlica.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Were those Roma of Muslim faith?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: And now could you please show Tegare to the Trial Chamber?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: [Witness points]

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: What was the ethnic makeup of the population of Tegare before the war?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: Half and half.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: In other words, it was a mixed population?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: I would now like to ask you to show the villages of Vranesevici. Could you perhaps mark the village of Vranesevici there? And then Stanatovici. It's just below -- it's just below Vranesevici if it is of any help, right. Kaludra. Polimci. Then Ratkovici. Ducici. Dvorista. Magudovici. Oparci. And could you also show us the area of Fakovici and the hamlets in that area, Popovici, Seona, and Mlecva. Thank you. As to this last group of villages that I asked you about and you've shown us from Vranesevici onwards, are those Muslim or Serb villages?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: They are 100 per cent Serb villages.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Could you show the Trial Chamber where Bradjevina is? Bradjevina is not marked on the map but could you more or less locate it on the map even though it's not marked?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: For the record, the witness places an X between Magudovici and Vranesevici which he alleges -- agrees to be Bradjevina.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Could you tell us how far Bradjevina is from your hamlet?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: Two and a half kilometres.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Is it as the crow flies or if you walk down the road?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: Down the road.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Is it closer as the crow flies?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: There is very little difference there.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, I'm going to ask you the following in relation to the position of these villages. Could you describe to the Trial Chamber what exactly the altitude of Bradjevina is in relation to your hamlet in Gornja Orlica? Could you tell us anything about that?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: For my village, the altitude is 300 metres, and Bradjevina, it's double that.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: In other words, Bradjevina is at an altitude which is higher than that of your village?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: How far is the village Ratkovici from your village?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: Four kilometres.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: And how far is Fakovici from your village?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: Four and a half kilometres.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: And now I'd like to ask you to show the Trial Chamber a number of other villages. Could you show us Orasici, if you can. Then Sikiric. Then Loznicka. And then Bjelovac. Could you tell the Trial Chamber what the ethnic makeup of those villages is? For example, Orasici and Loznicka to begin with?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: Orasici and Loznicka are 100 per cent Serb villages.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: And what about Sikiric and Bjelovac?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: Sikiric and Bjelovac are almost half and half. Actually, Bjelovac is mostly Serb, and Sikiric is 50/50.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: If we look at this entire area and take a comprehensive view of the area, could we say that the majority of the population of there area before the war was Serb or Muslim?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: It was Serb.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: As to your village, Zapolje and the hamlets of Zapolje including your hamlet of Gornja Orlica, could you say that they were surrounded by Serb villages before the war?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, we have already got an exhibit number but I would like to ask the usher to keep the map there because we are going to keep using it in the course of the entire testimony for this witness.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Tiro, was this a calm area until the end of the 80s?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: Yes. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Did the situation change in 1991?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Did things start to happen at night, which disturbed and gave cause for concern to the population in that area?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: Yes. Already in 1991, they started their training by the end of the year.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: How did you know that? Did you hear anything?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: Well, my sister and my cousin Memic Resad went to Trbajvina [phoen], and just behind them there were shots, and they even knew who actually fired those shots.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell me whether your sister tried to find out what was going on?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: Yes, she did. She asked one Serb man, "What's going on up there?" And he said, "Our people are having training in a place called Kecovina [phoen]. This is training for the reserve forces of both the army and the police."

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: You mentioned 1991. Was it by the end of the year?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Or was it in the beginning of 1991?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: Yes, it was at the end of 1991.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Did this -- was this event an isolated event or were there other similar events?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: Yes, there were other similar events.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Did it frighten the Muslim population of that area?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Tiro, I'm going to ask you to cast your mind back to January 1992. Did anything happen in your immediate surroundings in the Serb villages at that time?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: What was going on there then?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: Already in the month of January, the Serb Orlica, a part of had been Grabovacka Rijeka, people started wearing uniforms there and my neighbour, Zoran Jovanovic already had a specific hat on his head.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: You talked about these people who started wearing uniforms in January 1992. Were they Serbs? Is Zoran Jovanovic Serb?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, could I clarify the transcript, please? It said that it was a specific hat but in fact the witness said something more specific. He said he had a specific type of insignia which was a kokarde on his head.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Am I correct, witness, that you made a reference to a kokarde?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you, Witness. And thank you, Madam Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. But these people, you said started wearing uniforms as early as January 1992, did they have anything else?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: Well, yes. They had weapons.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: What type of weapons did they have?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: They had automatic rifles, M-48s and machine-guns.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Did you, in the course of March 1992, have any contact with any police force in the village called Gornja Orlica?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: What police force?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: The Serb police.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Did you yourself see any Serb police officers at the time?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Who did you see?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: I saw Zoran and Petko Jovanovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: So there were Serbs then, where were they from, those two?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: Zoran Jovanovic was from Srpska Orlica and Petko Jovanovic was from Grabovacka Rijeka.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Did you talk to them and if you did, what did they tell you?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: Well, we did talk to them and they said that they were setting up their Serb police force at Fakovici and that we no longer had anything to do with the municipality of Bratunac.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: In other words, they said that the Serb police would be competent for that area; did I understand you correctly?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Did they mention any municipality on that occasion?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: Yes. They told us that a new municipality was being set up, Skelani municipality.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Did you notice at that time, or shall I put it in another way. Did you in the course of March and April 1992 notice anyone being armed in that area?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Who?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: Serbs.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Could you tell the Trial Chamber what did you see exactly?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: We saw helicopters flying over Grabovacka Rijeka and my village as well as Ranesovici [phoen], towards Bradjevina, Magudovici, Ducici and they were transporting weapons there.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: The villages you mentioned, is that the general area of Ratkovici?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Could you describe the helicopters for the Trial Chamber? What did they look like? And were there any markings on them, if any?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: Yes. They were of dark green colour, military helicopters, with a red cross on them.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: As you said a minute ago, they were transporting weapons. How did you know what was it that they were transporting?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: We had a great friend of ours, a Serb. He was a great friend of the Muslims, and his name was Stojan.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: I'm sorry, the interpreter missed the last name.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Did he tell you anything?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: He would come to our village on a daily basis and he said that these helicopters were bringing weapons that are being distributed to the Serbs.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: The interpreter did not catch the name of this Serb friend of theirs. It was Stojan who?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Stevanovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. Sorry to have interrupted you.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: This Mr. Stojan Stevanovic, did he mention what sort of weapons they were?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: What did he say?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: He said that they were bringing in mortars, Zoljas, hand-held rocket launchers, and automatic and semi-automatic rifles as well as machine-guns.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Tiro, could you please go back to the map for a moment and show the Trial Chamber the road between Bjelovac and Fakovici.

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. For the record, the witness indicates by running along the road that flanks the Drina River on the Bosnian side, from Bjelovac right down to Fakovici.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation].

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Tiro, does that road pass by your house?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: That part that goes next to your house, how far is it actually from it?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: As the crow flies, about 200 metres.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Is it possible to see the road from your house?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: If one stood next to your house, what part of the road is visible? But first of all, let me ask you the following. Is the road higher in terms of altitude or lower than your house?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: Lower than my house.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: If one is to stand next to your house, what part of the road would be visible, if any?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: From Tegare almost to Fakovici. That's the part of the road that you can see down in the valley.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Could you also see a part of Grabovacka Rijeka?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: To a large extent.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. In April of 1992, did you reside in your village?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: In April of 1992, did you personally see something taking place on that road?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: What did you see? Could you tell the Trial Chamber.

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: I saw trucks, both military and civilian, going between Bjelovac towards Fakovici and back.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Could you see whether they were empty or loaded?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: We could see the civilian trucks and that they had no tarpaulin covers so we could see that they did carry some goods but we couldn't see what was in the military trucks because they were covered.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Could you see what it was that was on the civilian trucks?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: We were most interested in that, and we approached the road through a forest to see what it is they were transporting.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: What could you observe, if anything?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: On those civilian trucks, we saw heavy weaponry.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Please describe for the Trial Chamber what those heavy weapons were.

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: There were Pragas, antiaircraft guns, mortars, grenades, and ammunition crates.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Tiro, concerning this, another question for you: You said you've -- you were a member of the mountain infantry during your military term. At that time, were you acquainted with artillery weaponry?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: The things that you saw, how many trucks were there?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: I personally saw about a dozen. Or ten, to be precise.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: How long could you move freely in the area where you used to live, including the surrounding Serb villages?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: I could personally move about until the 3rd of May 1992.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Why did you mention that date, the 3rd of May 1992? Does that mean anything in particular for you?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: I remember that date clearly because there were no shops of ours remaining, and I went to Fakovici to buy flour, and I met with some of the horrific things that the Serbs were doing at the time.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: What did you see exactly and where? Where did you go, if you remember?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: Grabovacka Rijeka, the hamlet of Progon [phoen]. When I came there, and this is closely to Fakovici, I looked towards Drina, the Drina, and I saw a large vessel. They were transporting weapons across the Drina, and on this side, there were about 50 Serb soldiers in olive-drab uniforms awaiting the vessel and the weaponry.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: In relation to that, I have a question. You said there was a vessel, a boat. Can you tell us from what direction it came, because you were familiar with the area?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: So what was the direction that the vessel came from?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: It came from Bracevci [phoen] towards the Bosnian side.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Are Bacici [phoen] a place in Serbia?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Apart from that vessel, for which you said was transporting weapons, did you see anything else in Serbia?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: One could see Gornja Treznica [phoen] and that part of Serbia where they set up heavy weaponry, with their nozzles turned towards Muslim villages.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: When you said towards Muslim villages, which villages do you have in mind?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: Zapolje, the Muslim part of Tegare, Mocevici, and my hamlet of Gornja Orlica.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. You said you saw a vessel carrying weapons. Could you see what it was transporting?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: Yes. There were machine-guns, grenades in crates, and other infantry weapons, as well as ammunition.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: So you saw the crates?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: You said you could move freely until the 3rd of May 1992. Were you frightened by this event? Did you continue towards Fakovici or did Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. you return home?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: I went back home.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Did you, until April or the 3rd of May of 1992, go to Mocevici?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: Yes. On the 25th of April.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Why did you go there?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: Because I learned I could find and buy some flour up there.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: In order for you to reach Mocevici at that time, were you forced to go through any of the Serb villages?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Which one?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: I had to go next to Srpska Bradjevina.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: On that occasion, did you see anything close to Bradjevina?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: What did you see?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: I saw they set up in a pine forest some heavy weaponry.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Can you remember in what part of Bradjevina the weaponry was?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Could you tell the Trial Chamber where it was? Could you show it on the map that is in front of you?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: This is Bradjevacko Brdo and Magudovica Brdo.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Magudovica Brdo and Bradjevacko Brdo, are they close?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: They are actually linked.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: As you said, they set up heavy weaponry?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: What sort of heavy weaponry was it when it comes to Bradjevacko Brdo?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: There was an antiaircraft gun, as well as PAT, the so-called PAT.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: How about Magudovica Brdo?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: There was a Praga and two mortars.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: You said you went on a road. Was it possible for someone to see it from that road that you were on?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: The armour that was in Bradjevacko Brdo, that was very close to the road.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: How close or how far?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: Five to six metres.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Practically speaking it was right next to the road.

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: What did you do?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: I was about 50 metres away from it and I heard some conversation. I went below the road and went around towards Mocevici.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: If I understood you correctly, you went into the forest?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Were you able to observe where the weaponry was turned to?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: And what direction?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: Towards Mocevici.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: How about Magudovica Brdo?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: The nozzles were towards Poznanovici, Podkorjen.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: And the witness said another name of a village that the interpreter didn't catch.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. What was the name of the other village between Poznanovici and Podkorjen?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Tiro, could you repeat the names of the villages we were discussing some locations concerning weaponry at Magudovica Brdo. What were those villages?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: Those were Muslim villages. The nozzles were turned towards Poznanovici and Podkorjen.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Concerning those locations with heavy weaponry, were there any people to be seen there?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Did you recognise any of them?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Who?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: Stevo Stevanovic and Milo van Milanovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Where were those people from?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: From Bradjevina.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Are they Serbs?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Were there other people with them?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: There were a number of people there, but their backs were turned towards me.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. During the same period, that is the second half of April of 1992, could you see the area of Tuk?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: It is a part of Grabovacka Rijeka right next to my village.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. Did you observe anything there, if anything?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: What did you see?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: I saw machine-gun nests.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Were you alone when you saw them?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Please tell the Chamber who you were with?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: My brother-in-law, Mitici Sacir.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Were you worried by that situation? Were you trying to find as much detail about Serb positions, their weaponry?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: I was very interested in seeing that, to learn as much as possible.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Was that a reason --

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: That was the only reason.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Was that the reason why you went to Tuk?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Describe for the Trial Chamber what it was that you saw. What did those machine-gun positions look like?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: They were set up on the coast line towards the Drina. They cut down some trees and it looked like nests behind which they put -- they mounted machine-guns, and the nozzles protruded between the tree trunks.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Could you see the machine-guns?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: Yes, with the naked eye.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Did you see anything else next to the nests, ammunition or anything else?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: There was a lot of ammunition in crates.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Were any of the crates open?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Could you see if there were people next to the machine-gun nests?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: Yes, there were.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Could you recognise any of them?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: Yes, I could. Radivoje Sekulic and his brother Mikajlo Sekulic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Do you remember Milomir Andric and Micic, Slobodan?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: Yes, they are neighbours of mine.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Did you see them over there?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: I saw them in Gajevi.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: This place of Gajevi how far is it from Tuk?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: As the crow flies about a hundred metres up on a hill.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: What was the distance that you saw them from?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: I was about a hundred metres away.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I would kindly ask the usher to give D508 to the witness.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Before that, I would like to ask you the following. The people that you mention, Milomir Andric and Mica Slobodan, were they standing close to any of the weapons?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: Yes. They were standing close to a mortar.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Could you please take a look at this document. I showed it to you in your proofing, didn't I?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Could you please take a look at the cover page. It is -- it has a title of "Military conscripts list." Please take a look at the third page. It says NB -- MB platoon. ERN number is 01315598. Did you find that?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Please take a look at the names under numbers 6 and 9.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is page 01315598, and a clarification, if I may, for both the Chamber and the witness. These are usually documents in the format of A3, and they cannot fit on to a single page. The next following page 01315599 is actually the continuation of the previous page of 01315598, and one could look at it this way, if you could please look at me, and I would ask the witness to bear with me as well.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Please take a look at the people mentioned under 6 and 9. Andric, Milomir, and Micic, Slobodan. Are those the people that you mentioned?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Please look at the column number 6 on this page. There is a date of joining the JNA. This is the 18th of April 1992.

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: One moment. I want to make sure that we can -- 6. We are talking of Milomir Andric, son of Milenko, no?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Who is number 6.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: According to you, Madam Vidovic, in the third column, forget the third -- the third is 28 October 1956, Vranesevic, Bratunac. The fourth column is Bratunac. What is the fifth -- what does your fifth column, in the original language, read, please?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In the fifth column, it says, if you mean the column.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: The fifth column, yeah, which supposedly is rank --

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Rank, it says infantry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And a third PB soldier and then the date.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: That's the sixth column. I've precisely asked to you clarify all this because earlier on, I heard you say that in the sixth column, it says 18th April 1992. What I have in the English language, in the English, it says 1993.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: That's why I was --

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In the original, it says 1992, and it is clearly visible that number 2 was corrected. Thank you for directing my attention to it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Just for the record, if you can -- usher, I need to see on the ELMO the B/C/S page.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If I may be of assistance.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Ms. Vidovic can give us again the ERN number or you can lend us --

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 01315599.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I can offer further clarification. The next column states the date of entry, the 3rd of January 1993.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So one couldn't be registered in the book prior to joining the JNA.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. Yes. All right. We've seen it. We've seen it. And we can proceed. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Excuse me, Your Honour, I'm grateful for Madam Vidovic's assistance. We also have a problem with the document. On the second page, with ERN number 99, the first column, five, when we go down to six lines and compare that with the English translation, I believe it's not exactly clear to us what would be in that column, if we could help.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In the Bosnian language, it is clearly stated, "infantry." I invite the witness to confirm that.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. In relation to this I wanted to ask you the following --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Are you satisfied, Ms. Sellers?

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Your Honour, we understand that there was just an error in the translation, the English version. Is that what I imagine my Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. learned counsel is saying?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I'm not understanding that. The translation "infantry," here, in the English version, is a correct reflection, correct translation, of the corresponding word, which we have in the original document. That's how I understood it. In other words, in both documents, you have "infantry".

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Thank you, fine Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: The sixth person in the list, so if you look at the English translation, what may have a little bit confused us is the line before, which is empty. All right? But that's the fifth person, not the sixth person. All right.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: [Previous interpretation continues] ... grateful, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Ms. Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Tiro, you said that you served in the mountain infantry?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Now I'd like to ask you about the infantry in the former JNA at the time when you did your military service. Did that mountain infantry have any mortars at the time that you were there?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: They had all types of heavy weaponry.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you for clarifying this. And now I'm going to ask you something else. Do you remember the beginning of May 1992? Did you Muslims, in the beginning of May 1992, for any reason at any point stop going to Fakovici?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Can you explain the Trial Chamber why it happened? Could you please leave the map there with the witness.

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: In the beginning of May, two underage boys were captured by Serbs and they were taken to the command post at Fakovici.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Did you know those underage boys? Do you remember their names?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Who were they?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: Biser Isakovic and Ibro Mujic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: What happened to them in Fakovici? Do you remember?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: Yes. They were held there for an entire day. In the meantime --

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Can I just ask you whether you yourself talked to them upon their return?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Were they mistreated in any way there?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: Yes. They were all black and blue all over their bodies, their backs. They said that for no reason at all they were beaten up.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us how long they were kept there?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: Just one day.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: You told us that you talked to them. What exactly did they tell you?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: Yes, I did talk to them, because I was amongst the people who were there. We went to visit the children and see what had happened to them. And so they started telling us what had happened to them in Fakovici, that they were beaten up and that they saw soldiers.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: But just before we move on to that, I'd like to put another question to you. Did they tell you who captured them and who took them to that command post at Fakovici?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: Yes, they did. It was Zoran Jovanovic. He introduced himself as the deputy police commander at Fakovici. And Petko Jovanovic was the commander of the Serb police at Fakovici.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Where were those two people from?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: Zoran Jovanovic was from Srpska and Petko Jovanovic was from Grabovacka Rijeka.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: What else did those boys tell you?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: Well, they told us that they saw soldiers up there, that they were getting ready, making preparations for some kind of departure, and that they were getting on to buses. They were loading arms on to buses, and they were loading arms on to a truck, and the truck was the property of the agricultural cooperative in Fakovici and that's what they were doing. They were loading ammunitions and weapons on to the truck and they went in the direction of Skelani.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: What did they tell you? Did they describe the appearance of those people, what clothes were they wearing?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: They were wearing camouflage uniforms.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: What about the two boys? Did they tell you anything specific whether they came back? Did they have a message for the Muslims of the area?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: Yes, they did. As of the 12th of May 1992, we should all surrender to the Serb army and we should all relinquish our arms.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Tiro, in relation to this, I'd like to ask you the following question. You mentioned Skelani a short while ago. Do you remember whether in the course of 1992, in the course of the war, you ever had the opportunity to talk to any Muslim refugees from any of the Skelani villages?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Do you remember anyone in particular?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: Yes. I do remember Vehbija Skaljic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Where is he from?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: He is from Tokoljaci.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: What did he tell you in the course of your conversation that might refer to Fakovici, in case he did say something?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: Well, I myself asked him what was going on up there. And he said to me the Fakovici command, people entered Skelani and they were sowing destruction all over. They were torching and destroying things and they were raping women, taking them away, and I asked him where to and he said, "I don't know."

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Just a moment, Mr. Tiro. We clarify this last bit of information? It says in the transcript that he said that "the Fakovici command." Did I understand you correctly that you said that "the people who had come from Fakovici"?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: Yes, thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Fine. Did he on that occasion --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Sorry to interrupt you, Ms. Vidovic. When did this conversation with this Muslim from Skelani take place? Because you just mentioned 1992. Which part of 1992?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] By the end of May.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. May I just put another question to you? Did Mr. Skaljic on that occasion in the course of your conversation, make any reference to the fact that at Tokoljaci he might have seen or recognised the person from Fakovici?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: What did he say exactly?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: He told me that he recognised the driver of the bus, whose name was Tico, but his nickname was Macedonian, and he used to live in Fakovici.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much, Your Honours, now I'm going to move on to another area so it might be convenient to have a break at this point, if you agree.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. Of course, Madam Vidovic. We'll have a 25-minute break starting from now which means we will reconvene at 10 to 11.00 Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. I recognise Ms. Sellers.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Yes, thank you, Your Honours. I've just been asked to convey by Mr. Wubben, first of all thanks for your concern for his health but secondly in terms of the 92 bis motions that the Prosecution of course will preserve the position until the filing of the motion.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. Okay. Thank you. When I said earlier I was referring to filing that -- on the 15th of August, more or less and that was subject of course to confirmation from Mr. Wubben because that was how I was reading that document. All right. Yes, Madam Vidovic, you may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Tiro, I hope that you still have the map from before. Can you show the Trial Chamber the location of the place called Ruljevici? I don't think that it is indicated on the map because it's a very small village indeed, but could you perhaps locate it on the map anyway and could you please mark it with an R?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: One moment, Madam Vidovic. The witness has indicated -- has put an R in the space between Grabovacka Rijeka and Vranesevici. Yes, thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: And in this respect, Mr. Tiro, I'm going to ask you for what this place Ruljevici was known before the war?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: The place Ruljevici was known for its old primary school, because that school covered those Serb villages. It was the only school for those villages.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Do you mean the area of Ratkovici. Ratkovici, Bradjevina, Kaludra, Anesovici [phoen]?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much for this clarification. Do you remember if anything happened to that school at any point in time before the war?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Could you tell the Trial Chamber what exactly it was?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: About two years before the war, the school was closed down and the children were sent to school in Fakovici.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Did you know for what reason the school was closed?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: Yes. That school was turned into a military facility.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: When you say military facility, do you mean a military facility for the JNA?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: No. A military facility for the Serb people and the Serb military.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Right. How do you know that the school was turned into a military facility on the basis of what can you claim that?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: Because we had already noticed them meeting even before the war. I mean, all those villages in the area were Serb villages and they were holding meetings and they also had some kind of training.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: One moment. I need to clear this because the witness said that this school was converted into a military facility two years before the war. I need you to specify exactly, therefore, whether, by April of 1990, 1990, this school had already been converted into a military facility.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Right. Before the presiding Judge asked you this question, you mentioned that there was a military training going on there. On the basis of what did you claim that?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: Because we could hear shooting.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Is it something that was widely known to villagers of the whole area, if you can tell us?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: Yes, everybody knew.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Before the war, did you ever know or have you ever met Mr. Zivko Prokic?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: Yes, I knew him very well.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Could you tell the Trial Chamber anything about the character of that man?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: He was an exceptionally good man. We were very good and very close friends, and he was very good to all Muslims.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Zivko Prokic is a Serb, isn't he?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: Yes, he's a Serb.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Did you have any contacts with Mr. Zivko before the war?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: Yes. Very often.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: In what way?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: We helped one another.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Could you please testify the Trial Chamber where Mr. Zivko Prokic used to live?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: Zivko Prokic used to live in the village of Ruljevici. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: How far was his land from the school in Ruljevici, the school that we've mentioned earlier on?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: Just 20 metres across the river, or away from the river.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. Did I understand you correctly in that you said that the only dividing line between his land and the school was the river?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: Yes, just the river.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Did you meet with him at some point in mid-April 1992?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: For what reason?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: It was the spring season, and we had to sow our crops, and I helped him with his fertilisers in mid-April. I was with him --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Sellers?

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Your Honour, I just want to ask is it possible that he mentioned the name or testify about what is the name of the river from where he's described the village on our map, the river that I would indicate would be the Drina River. Can we just put the name of the river?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, certainly. Mr. Tiro, you've heard Madam Sellers's comment. Could you give us the name of the river, please?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour. The name of the river is Grabovacka Rijeka.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. One moment, Madam Vidovic. Judge Eser?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ESER
utterances.text: Just a question with regard to the size of this village. It's rather unusual that it's not on the map. What is the size of this village, Ruljevici, as compared to Bjelovac or your own home place?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It was the same size as my own village. It had somewhere between 15 and 17 houses.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, if I may I'd just like to clarify.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Madam Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Many small villages and hamlets are not indicated on the map because this is a one-100.000 map, just for the sake of clarification. Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Now, I'm going to put the following question to you, sir. You've told us that you had met with this man at some point in the middle of April 1992. Did you actually go and visit him on his land?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Did you see anything on that day from his land?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: Yes, I did. I saw things very clearly.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Let me just put the question to you first. From that land, from that part of the field that you were working on, were you able to see the area of the school and the surroundings of the school?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: Yes. The schoolyard and the access to the school as well.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: When you talk about access, you mean access from what direction?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: From Ratkovici, Validovici [phoen], Bradjevina, Ducici, Kaludra, Polimici, all those villages that gravitate towards Ratkovici.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: So you could see their access way to the school?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: Yes, the direct access to the school.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. What else did you see around the school? Actually, what did you see on that day?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: I saw large numbers of uniformed people.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: When you talk about large numbers, how many do you mean? Can you assess that?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: About 300 people.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: What were those people wearing?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: They were wearing uniforms, camouflage uniforms.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Right. Do you remember if they were carrying anything?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: Yes, they were carrying weapons.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell the Trial Chamber what sorts of weapons they had?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: They had automatic and semi-automatic weapons, M-48s and machine-guns.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Were you able to see who those people were? Where were they from?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: Yes, for the most part. The ones I knew because they were all my neighbours.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Have I understood you correctly in that you've just said that those were people from the surrounding Serb villages?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Did you know any of those people?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: Yes, I did know quite a few of them.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Do you remember what was the thing that you noticed first on that day?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: Yes. I remember a group -- well, there were several groups which separated in front of the school. They went into this creek, and they were doing shooting exercises there.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Can you remember any event to do with Mr. Andrija Ilic?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: Yes, Andrija Ilic is somebody I could see very clearly.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Where was he from?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: Grabovacka Rijeka. He came in front of the school in Ruljevici and I heard some noise around the school, and he was being told to get a weapon, and he was saying, "I don't want a gun, and I'm going to throw it into the water anyway."

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: For how long did you actually stay and observe what was going on?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: For about half an hour.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Where exactly were you observing it from?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: From about 20 metres ago behind the tree next to the river.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Was Mr. Zivko any way near you?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: Zivko was 15 metres away from me.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: You told us that you knew most of those people. Do you remember recognising any -- anyone in particular?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: In this respect, Your Honour, I had the intention of showing you a video, D97, but we are having some technical problems. So instead of doing that I'm going to be using a photo, which is a Defence Exhibit, D96, so I would like to ask the usher to show this Defence Exhibit to the witness.
