I would just like to clarify to the Trial Chamber that this photo is a part of a video which was exhibit D97, D97, which was filmed on the 15th of December 1992. Mr. Tiro, I would like to you take a look at the face of this man. Do you recognise this person?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Who is it?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: This is Mr. Ilic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Did you say Novo Ilic?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell me where this person's from?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: From the centre of Bjelovac.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: One moment, please. I want to make sure that there is no confusion here. We are having the word Novo Ilic now. Before, I heard him say Andrija, Andrija Ilic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, he did mention Andrija Ilic with regard to a fight. It's somebody else. It's not the same person that we can see here. Could you just say the name of this person very clearly?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: Jovo Ilic Bjelovac.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Just for the transcript, it is Novo Ilic, N-O-V-O, from Bjelovac.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Do you know the Ilic family?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: I do know them very well.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Can you explain to the Trial Chamber how come you know people from Bjelovac?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: I know Novo's brother.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: No. Before we go on to say that, I would just like to put a general question to you. How do you know people from Bjelovac? Is there any special reason why you know so many people from Bijelovac?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: Yes, there is; because I went to primary school at Bjelovac.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, I'd like you to answer the next question about the Ilic family. Do you know anyone else from that family?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: I know his brother, who is called Stojan Ilic, and his nickname is Kole and I know Rado Ilic as well. He's also his brother.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Right. And in this respect, I'd like to ask you the following. Did you see that person in Ruljevici on that occasion?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: Yes, I saw him and I saw his brothers as well.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Since we are talking about the Ilic brothers, can you tell me whether you remember any events from April 1992 that had anything to do with any of the Ilic brothers?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: Yes. I do remember about the end of April, Novo's brother Stojan Ilic called Kole came to buy firewood from my cousin, Resad Memic, and he came with his own truck. When he came into the village, he opened the door, and -- I mean he opened the door of his truck and we could see that he had weapons, he had an automatic rifle and a gun in his truck.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Now I'd like the witness to be shown the Defence Exhibit D254. D254. It is a list from the Territorial Defence of Bjelovac, the draftees per squad and from 1992 and I'd like the witness to look at the document. On the page where we've got the list of names and the number is 01320441. I would like to you take a look at the names: Number 1, Ilic, Stevo, Stojan. 3, Ilic, Stevo, Novo. And number 32, Ilic, Stevo, Rade. Did you see those names?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Are these the people that you were referring to earlier?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Is Stevo their father? Could you take another look at this list? And could you tell us whether you know anyone else whose name is on the list?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Who do you know?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: Stojanovic, Ivan.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Just a moment. Is it number 16? And who else do you know?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: Ignjatovic, Srecko, Goran.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Okay. Have you got any knowledge about the other two persons you mentioned that are on the list?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Did you learn anything from the Muslims in Bjelovac about these people and, if so, when?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: Yes. This Goran Ignjatovic was a great nationalist.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Did you say Mihajlovic?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: Ignjatovic, number 30. Mihajlovic, Srecko, Goran.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Could you look under number 30?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: Yes. Mihajlovic, Srecko, Goran, a nationalist even before the war, and especially at the beginning of the war. He provoked Muslims in Bjelovac.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Could you tell the Chamber who told you about this Goran person?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: Salko Golic [phoen] from Bjelovac.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: When Mr. Lolic discussed some people from Bjelovac with you, on the eve of the war, did he mention something about uniforms or the weapons of those people?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: Yes. He said that they were all uniformed in Bjelovac and that they had weapons.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Could you please turn to the next page? We will make a small digression.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, if I may have a moment. I'm finished with this document. I would kindly ask the usher to show the witness another document. That is the list of persons from VP 2465/5, pay for official trip and pay for July 1992, the page number is 01335377. I showed you this document during proofing, didn't I?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Please take a look at the list of the TO in Tegare and Orlica. Do you see the names of the people there? Do you know any of the names?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: I know all of them.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Do you remember if you saw any of these people in Ruljevici on that occasion, the occasion that you've described a minute ago?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Could you tell the Chamber who is it that you saw?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: Jovanovic, Zoran. Drago Jovanovic. But he's not on the list, as far as I can see. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Could you please stay with the list. Take a look at number 2711. Take a close look at the list and tell us who is it that you saw?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: Zoran Jovanovic. Ilic, Radivoje. Milenko Andric. And Dobrivoje Prokic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: All right. Could you tell me where these people are from? Are they from Tegare and Orlica?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. When you saw those people in Ruljevici on that occasion, what were they wearing?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: Olive-drab uniforms.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Did they have weapons?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Please go on to the next page of the document. You can see here that it says, "TO Vranesevici." Please take a look at the names. Do you know them? Or rather, did you know them before the war?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: Yes, they were all my neighbours.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: All right. Did you see any of these people on that occasion in Ruljevici?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Who?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: Jovanovic, Vitomir. Pero Prokic, Stanko Prokic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Were they also uniformed -- in uniforms and wearing weapons?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: Yes, all of them.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, could we assign this document an exhibit number?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. Madam Vidovic, this will become Defence Exhibit D728.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We kindly ask the usher to put another document before the witness. This is a Defence Exhibit, number D49, list of fighters from Fakovici, their salaries for the months of September, October, and November, the date mentioned is the 25th of January 1993.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Could you please take a look at the list and tell us if you know these people?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: I just want to make sure. Do you have before you the list of fighters from Fakovici, in handwriting?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Did you see any of the people mentioned on this list on that occasion in Ruljevici?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Could you tell the Chamber who did you see?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: Milan Ilic. Tanjo Bogicevic. Petko Milanovic. Stanisa Stevanovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Anyone else?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: You mentioned Stanisa Stevanovic. Can you remember if he was carrying a weapon on that occasion?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: When I was in the field, Stanisa was coming from Ratkovici and Bradjevina and the other Serb villages, followed by about 100 people.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Can you remember specifically whether he was carrying a weapon?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: Yes. He was carrying a PM.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: What does PM mean?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: Machine-gun.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: I would kindly ask the usher to put another document before the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, one moment, Madam Vidovic. Judge Eser?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ESER
utterances.text: Before we leave this exhibit, I just have a question to clarify whether the dating is correct in the English version. It says the 25th of January 1993. And if we look to the Bosnian version, it could also be read 25th of September, 1993. Even if you go further down with Milanovic, Petko, it reads like 9-9-93. I'm no expert in handwriting but --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: The thing is this, if I may given my assistance here, because Judge Eser's comment is very pertinent. We are dealing with a document which, in the English translation, carries the date at the top 25th of January 1993, but we -- the document deals with salaries allegedly paid to fighters from Fakovici for the months of September, October, and November. So to me, we are dealing with a document which, if it's dealing with September, October, and November, it could be September, October and November of 1992. And the date of the document would, indeed, be 25th of January 1993 because, if we are dealing with a document which is dated 25th of September of 1993, I don't think it would deal with the payment of salaries of the following two months. I mean, that's at least from -- following the line of other documents I have seen. So I don't know. I mean, I can't be of any further help because I didn't write this document myself, but --

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, if I may be of assistance, we have a similar discussion regarding a previous document, and you are right, exactly. This document, as many other similar documents, bears the date of the 25th of January, but it obviously deals with the salaries that were -- that refer to an earlier period. So you are completely right, and this is the way I interpreted it as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: That's the way I understand it but of course I stand to be corrected. By all means, because --

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would just like to say for the Prosecution's part we understand that that's the manner in which the Defence is choosing to use the document. We have no indication at this point whether it was to foresee salaries that were to be paid or it's only speaking retrospectively. That's our only comment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. Let's go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, what is important for the Defence at this moment is that the witness is testifying on the names of the people he saw in Ruljevici, wearing uniforms and carrying weapons in 1992 and this is what is important to us. Thank you. If the witness could please take a look at the following document, which is the list of fighters for VPB Fakovici on the 3rd of April 1993.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, please take a look at the names, and there are some markings here, and then go to the next page, which states, "the 2nd Company." Under number 1, there is a name, Stanisa Stevanovic. Could you tell the Chamber what PM next to his name means?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: Machine-gun.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, could this document be assigned an exhibit number, please?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. This will become Defence Exhibit D729, Madam Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Tiro, we will now go again back to that day in Ruljevici, because it is very important. You told us you know all of those people including Stanisa Stevanovic. For how long before that did you know him?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: My entire life.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: How come?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: Because we were close neighbours.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Was he particularly close in good relations with any of your relatives?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: Yes. He would come to our village, but he was a great friend of a family member of mine, Mr. Njemic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: One moment, Madam Vidovic, because I want to make this clear, since you are focusing on this particular individual. Is this the individual which is -- in this document appears behind the number 2, in the second part? The first Ceta, or is it someone else?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, second platoon, number 1.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. That's correct. Okay. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction, second company.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Second company, second Ceta. This is on second page, the second page of the document.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And he is -- on that page.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: I asked you about Stanisa Stevanovic. What did you know about him from before the war?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: He was rather extreme in his views. He liked to provoke, not only Muslims but Serbs as well.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Could you tell the Chamber whether you know if he belonged to any political party before the war?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Which one?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: The Radical Party, Seselj's party.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: How do you know that?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: At the beginning of April, my uncle saw him having lunch with Radisa Jovanovic, with Seselj in the Brioni hotel, near Ljubovija.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Did anything else take place before the war in relation to him?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: Yes. He killed his relative, Bogdan Milanovic, over a plot of land.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Was there a fight?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: The other person was an elderly one. He hit him once and died on the spot.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Do you know if criminal proceedings were instigated?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: Yes. And he was convicted.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Could you describe his character from what you knew of him?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: It is difficult to describe it. He was a nationalist, an extremist, and had he been given any position of authority, he would destroy everyone.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Could you tell us of his relations with his family before the war? Were there any disputes within his own family, apart from the murder?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: Yes. With his entire family.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: With who exactly?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: With another relative, Stojan Stevanovic, then with his uncle and they are still in dispute. This uncle is Miloje Jovanovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: On what do you base your assertion when you say he's still in dispute with his uncle, Dzilo Jovanovic?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: I went there recently to my village and I was met there by his uncle Dzilo. He greeted me and burst into tears. He told me, "My brother Hamed, I can no longer stand this. Stanisa wants to take all of my land away."

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: I will now go back to the event in Ruljevici, when you saw Stanisa Stevanovic. You saw that there was a large group of people with him. Where were they from, those people in the group?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: Bradjevina, Magudovici, Polimci, and the upper part of Ratkovici.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Among those people, did you recognise anyone else?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Who exactly?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: I recognised Stevo Stevanovic. I recognised Milenko Stevanovic, Ljubisa Gajic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would kindly ask the usher to put a photograph in front of the witness. We received this photograph and we signed the receipt. This is photograph number 88 from the OTP. And the number is 02028798. To clarify the transcript, the number of the photograph is 020287898/22. Hyphen 22. I need to repeat it again.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: You don't need to.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] All right.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Could you please take a look at the photograph? Do you recognise a person on it.

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Who is it?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: Milenko Stevanovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Did you know him from before the war?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: You can see him standing in front of his house. I'm sorry, in front of a house. Do you know what the house is?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: Yes. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Could you keep the photograph, please. We'll go back to it in detail. Now I want to ask you the following. Did you know Milenko Stevanovic well?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: What was he like?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: A great nationalist. It was very difficult for him to greet a Muslim.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Would you greet you?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: No. Whenever we would pass by, we never exchanged greetings.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Do you know anything about his role in the events in Srebrenica in July 1995?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Could you tell the Chamber what is it that you know?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: My neighbour, told me when we left Srebrenica.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: A question before that. Did you know whether he was a Serb army member?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: Yes. He was a commander.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: A commander of what?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: A company commander.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Could you now go on and tell us what you intended to? What did you hear? What is your knowledge of his actions in July of 1995?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: My neighbour was in Potocari with all the other people and we went the other way. He came to Potocari, and not just him but Stanisa Stevanovic, Petko Prokic, and Stanko Prokic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Could you pause a moment, please. Did this lady tell you any details about the people she saw and, if she did, could you tell us her name?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: Yes. Hajda Huremovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: What else did Ms. Huremovic tell you?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: He told her to take off her sweater because it was green. She commented, she said that that was the colour of Muslims.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Was there a man close to her?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: Yes. Munib Hasic, a neighbour.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: What happened next?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: He got on the bus, but he took him off the bus, he took him away, and nothing is known of his whereabouts now.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: When you say this Milenko, you mean Milenko Stevanovic?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Is Ms. Huremovic alive?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, could we assign an exhibit number to this photograph of Milenko Dzanovic [phoen] and it could stay with the witness because I intend to go back to it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Vidovic. This document or this photo which on the screen appears in colour, but a copy of which we have received in black and white, is being marked as Defence Exhibit D730.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Tiro, in your evidence you stated that you stayed in Ruljevici for about half an hour. Did you leave that place after that?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Why?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: This neighbour and a friend of mine, Zivko, told me that it was dangerous to stay there and that I have to leave that part of Ruljevici and his property.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Did you do that?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: Yes. I couldn't use the road. Rather, he took me from Ruljevici towards Grabovica via a shortcut in the forest, and he escorted me so that I could get there safely.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. In your evidence, you mentioned that the Serbs from the Fakovici command issued an ultimatum to surrender your weapons until the 12th of May of 1992?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: To who did that ultimatum pertain to?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: Muslims.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Of what villages?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: Zapolje and my hamlet of Gornja, and Tegare, the Muslim part of Tegare.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Could you please tell the Chamber the following: The Muslims in Zapolje and in Orlica, were they armed?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: Just two rifles, one automatic and another semi-automatic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Who were the people who had those rifles?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: Razim Sezanovic [phoen], he had the automatic rifle because he was the active policeman and the other person was Sevel Husic [phoen]. He had this semi-automatic rifle and he was in the reserve police force.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. What was the situation like in the Muslim part of Tegare? Were they armed?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: Yes, they had hunting rifles. They were all members of their hunter society.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: How many of them approximately?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: Around -- about a dozen.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Did you turn over the two rifles you had to the Serbs in relation to that ultimatum?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: What did you do?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: All of the families and the children and the elderly fled towards Mocevici and in the forest, in the environs of the villages.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: On the 12th of May of 1992, in the forests around Mocevici, were there many people in your estimate?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: Thousands of them.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Where were those people from?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: From Voljavica all the way up to Josava.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Did I understand correctly that the villagers from your hamlet joined as well?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: Yes. It included all Muslim villages between Josavici and Voljavica and they moved towards the Drina.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Did your co-villagers join the group close to Mocevici?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: You mentioned the Drina villages -- the Muslim villages along the River Drina. Did you in May and June 1992 get to talk to those people and, if so, what did they tell you?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: Yes. I spoke with people from various villages, and they told us about the torching, the killings, people being taken away to camps, about the rapes. I can't actually prove that I was not an eyewitness myself but that's what I heard, from those people, and many of those people have gone missing as well.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Now I'd like the usher to show a document to the witness. It is the document number 04276217. It's the Brigade command of the Serb armed forces in Birac and the date is the 31st of May 1992, at Sekovici. It is an order, in fact.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: And, Mr. Tiro, I'm going to read out you the most relevant bit of this which reads, "Pursuant to the decision of the Birac SAR, Serb Autonomous Region, Birac which regulates the moving out of the Muslim population from the territory of the Serb autonomous region Birac, I hereby order to set up a camp in Vlasenica and secure it in compliance with international regulations. I another bid any arbitrary decision on the physical liquidation of prisoners." Mr. Tiro, I'm going to ask you the following questions. These refugees that you told us about, did they ever mention any camps that the Serbs would take them to from the area of Podrinje?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us which once?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: Susica, Vlasenica, Gradina, Sase, and the Vuk Karadzic school in Bratunac.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Your Honour, I'd like this document to be attributed to an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. This document will become Defence Exhibit 731.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation].

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Tiro, let me ask you where you yourself were in 12th of May 1992?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: I accompanied my family at a distance of about a hundred metres from my house. It was a dense pine forest.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Where is that forest?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: Between my Orlica, Gornja Orlica, and Srpska Orlica.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Were you on your own or were there other people there?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: There were five more people.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Do you remember their names?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: I do. They were all my cousins.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Could you tell us their names?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: My brother, Mehmed Tiro. My cousin, Rasid Memic, Nedzad Memic, Habib Memic and Zahudin Herinovic [phoen].

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: What did you do on that occasion?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: We wanted to find out why there was this ultimatum and what they were going to do with our goods.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: How big is the place where you said you were hiding and how far is it away from your houses?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: A hundred metres away.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: From that area, did you have a good view of the area around your houses?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: What could you see?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: We could see, after 3.00, that the Serb soldiers were coming from the direction of Fakovici, Grabovacka Rijeka, and other soldiers were coming from the other side, from Tegare and Srpska Orlica.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: And what happened next? What did you see?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: The ones from Fakovici and Grabovacka Rijeka, up there, they entered the village. The Roma part of the village of Orlica. And they started shooting. They opened fire. And they torched first of all Suljo Osmanovic's house, and then Salecin Isakovic's [phoen] house as well.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Did you see what the other group coming from the other direction was doing?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: Yes. That other group came and entered the other end of the village, and first of all they started shooting in the direction of the village and the houses and then they set Derusa [phoen] Mujanovic's house on fire.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: And did they stop there? Did they just torch those three houses or what happened next?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: Well, they continued on both sides and they torched 30 houses.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Did I understand you correctly in that we are talking about 30 Muslim Roma houses?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Tiro, from where you were, were you able to recognise any of the Serbs, any of the attackers?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: Yes. They were all neighbours from the road.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Just a moment. Who did you recognise?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: From the Fakovici, Grabovacka Rijeka direction, the leader was Vitomir Jovanovic, and then there was Milan Arsenovic, Radivoje Sekulic, Petko Sekulic, and Mihajlo Sekulic carrying a machine-gun.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Right. And what about the other group of people? Did you recognise anyone there?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Who?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: Zoran Jovanovic and Drago Jovanovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Is it the same person, I mean Zoran Jovanovic, the one that you mentioned participated in the capture of those two young boys who had been taken to the command post at Fakovici?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I would like the witness to be shown the Exhibit D48. It is a list from TO Grabovacka Rijeka, Vranesevici, and the number is 00656808.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Could you please take a good look at this exhibit? And I would also like to ask you something else first. Vranesevici and Grabovacka Rijeka, are they a part of the local community in Fakovici?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Good. Could you take a look at the list of names here? You mentioned in the course of your testimony a number of names. For example, number 2, Jovanovic, Vitomir. Is it the person you said you saw in Orlica on the 12th of May 1992? Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Number 12 and number 30 -- no, number 12 and 13, Radivoje Sekulic and Petko Sekulic. Are they the people you mentioned?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Number 7, Milan Arsenovic?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: And now, Mr. Tiro, I would like to draw your attention to the bottom part of the document, which says, "For TO Vranesevici, Prokic, Stanija." Did you know this man before the war?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Do you know anything about his activities before the war, if there was any activity on his part, and did you see him on any occasion?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: One moment, Madam Vidovic. Can we have the list put on the ELMO, please? Thank you. Yes. Sorry to have interrupted you, Madam Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. Which --

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Could you just put the document a little higher up on the screen so that we can see the signature? Right. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Which is the part which says --

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It says "on behalf of Vranesevici."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: [Previous interpretation continues] ... TV. I don't know if this is -- this is a mistake in the transcript, but if you go to page 64, line 23, the last three lines, "Now, Mr. Tiro, I'd like to draw your attention to the bottom part of the document which says" --

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Basically what we have in the English text. That's why I want a clarification. What we have in the English text says: "Note from April to today these people received just one salary." But in the transcript, it is -- it says "for TV" --

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I don't know what that means.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, it's a mistake in the Bosnian original. It says on behalf of the TO Territorial Defence of Vranesevici, Stanoje Prokic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. That clears things up. So --

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And this note that you've read out is just above the signature. And now I was talking to the witness about the role played by Stanoje Prokic, and I was asking the witness if he had ever seen him on any occasion before the war.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Where?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: Yes at Ruljevici in front of the school.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell me do you remember what he was doing on that occasion?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: He was standing there in the perimeter of the school and he was greeting people who were arriving, and I saw him greeting Stanisa Stevanovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And now I'm going to refer you back to the events of the 12th of May 1992, the events in Orlica. Do you remember whether, on the 12th of May 1992, anyone was killed in Orlica? Did you see or find out about anyone having been killed in that day?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Was anyone killed and, if so, who was it?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: Yes. An elderly couple was killed. Ajdan Mujanovic [phoen], who was 80 years old and his wife, Tina Mujanovic, she was also 80. They were slaughtered with a knife. And their grandson was there. He didn't want to leave. And he was captured and he is still missing to this day.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Tiro, did you yourself see the dead bodies of those people?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: Yes, I myself went and buried the bodies together with a relative of theirs when he came back.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. On that same day, did the Serbs attack the part of the village where you lived, Gornja Orlica, that is?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: What was going on there afterwards? I mean, were they in control of that area?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: They were carrying out checks and controls in all those Muslim villages which were in their vicinity.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: What did you do? Did you nevertheless try and enter your village and, if so, for what reason?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: We used to hide in the woods during the day and during the night we would go back and get our food, our supplies that we had buried, in order to be able to survive.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Whilst you were wandering around the woods in Orlica, where was your family? Could you tell the Trial Chamber who were your dependents, so to say?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: I had an elderly and sick mother. I had two sisters, a brother who is an invalid, and I had a daughter-in-law with her three children, and also a brother-in-law and his sister and their two children.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Were they all living in a house of some sort, or were they all out in the open with the other refugees?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: No. We did not even have enough space in any houses. Quite a few people, actually thousands of people, were out in the open, in the woods.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Does that include your family as well?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: Yes. My family was outdoors non-stop.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: You told us that you used to walk around -- travel around that area. Where were you at around the 28th of May 1992?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: On the 98th -- on the 28th of May, 1992, I was in the vicinity of my village. I was perhaps 50 metres away out in the woods, and -- where there was a quarry. That's where I was hiding.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Did you observe what was going on in your village?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: Yes. The same people came again from both sides, and they entered my village.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: When you say the same people, do you mean the Serbs from Grabovacka Rijeka, the ones you mentioned before, from Vranesevici as well?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: Yes, from Srpska Orlica and Tegare.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Sellers?

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Your Honour, Defence counsel has tried to clarify, the same people, the same --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Tiro, when you say that they were the same people who carried out the attack on the 12th of May, what is the basis for your claim?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: It's on the basis of the fact that I saw them and I recognised them on that occasion once again. I also saw them and recognised them on the 28th of May in 1992, and that was with reference to those 30 houses once again.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Well, can you tell us what actually happened on the 28th of May?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: On the 28th of May, they first plundered our houses and they then proceeded to destroy and torch them as well.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Was your house torched on that occasion as well?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Could you tell me, first of all, what was the month of June like in that year? Do you remember?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: It was very rainy. There was not a lot of sun.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Right. Do you remember what state those refugees, including your own family members, were in, out in the forest?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: They were in a terrible state. They had no food, they had no blankets, they had no shelter.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: What happened to your mother? First all, rather, how old is your mother?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: My mother at that stage was 62 years old.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: What happened to her by the end of June 1992?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: By the end of June 1992, she fell ill. She was exhausted. And because it was too cold and rainy and we did not have any food, and on the 4th of July she actually died.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Was she an exception or were other people falling ill and dying amongst the refugees?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: Quite a few fell ill or starved simply and died.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Were there any doctors there or anyone else who could help those thousands of people out in the woods?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Apart from the problems you've just mentioned that those people were encountering, such as disease, cold, hunger, was the area of Mocevici under attack at any point and in any way, in that period of time, that is to say June of 1992?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: In what way?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: Yes. There were heavy weaponry attacks, shelling, infantry attacks as well. Mocevici was under attack.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell me about those thousands of people who were hiding in the woods? Were they under attack?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: Yes, of course they were, they were very exposed because they were out in the open they had no where to hide.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Were those people being wounded and killed because of those artillery attacks?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: Yes, many people. Many people were wounded and many people were killed.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Do you know anything about where the attacks were being launched from?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: Yes. The attacks were coming from Bradjevina, Magudovici, and Ratkovici.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: What is the basis for this claim?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: The fact that I was just above my village and I was standing in the forest. So it was at a higher altitude and we could hear the noise and then there was a flash, always, and strong explosions, powerful explosions.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell the Trial Chamber what the altitude was?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: Where I was?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: No, no, no. Where the area was?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: It is Kosa Urbine.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Tiro, in this respect, may I ask you whether the Muslims in that area, or you yourself were very interested in finding out what was going on amongst the Serbs and what weapons they had, and where they were shooting from? Were you trying to find that out?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: Yes, of course we were always interested in that because we were trying to find the best way of protecting ourselves.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Right. Can you tell me whether you know about any infantry fighting having taken place by the end of June 1992 or, to be even more specific, do you know what happened in the second part of June 1992 in the area of Tegare?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: Yes. The Muslim part of Tegare was attacked and I heard shots being fired.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: I'm just going to interrupt you there. When that happened, were you yourself in the area and can you tell us, can you tell the Trial Chamber, what part of Tegare are we referring to, the Serb or the Muslim part?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: I'm referring to the Muslim part of Tegare. And I was just above Tegare and I went there because I wanted to flee in the direction of Zapolje because it was a bit safer there and so I want to hide in that area. And then they were attacking the Muslim part of Tegare.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Just a moment, Mr. Tiro. On that day, and as far as you know, was there any Muslim from the Muslim part of Tegare taken prisoner?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: Yes. Riza Sanojevic [phoen], but he's not from Tegare; he's from Zapolje.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Right. What happened to him? Did you ever talk to this person?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: Yes. He was released on the same day, at dusk.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: And did you meet him on the same day?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: Yes, in Zapolje, in his village.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: What did he tell you?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: He told me that he was captured by Vilomir Petrovic, who was called Veljo, and he wanted to take him to the Serb command post at Fakovici. And then Velisav Petrovic came along and he had a fight with his brother Velimir and he let Riza go and he let him go back to his own village.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Did he mention witnessing any other Serbs alive or dead on that occasion? Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: Yes. He saw two dead Serbs at Tegarska Reka.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Right. Did he tell you their names? Do you remember?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Whose names did he mention?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: Milovan Micic and Radovan Ivanovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Right. Now I'd like to ask the usher to show the witness the exhibit 0435987 -- 875. The list of killed fighters at the area of Fakovici, Voljevici, and Tegare. So could you please look at the name on the list, number 2, and then number 3. Are they the people you mentioned?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please assign an exhibit number to this document? I'd also like to show something else to the witness. It is the Defence Exhibit --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: In the meantime, this will become Defence Exhibit D732. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. I'd like to ask the usher to show the witness the Defence Exhibit D45, D45. It is a list of killed fighters from the VP military post 7042, Bratunac. It's a bulky document, and I'm going to ask you to just look at the relevant bits of that document.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Could you turn to the page starting with the number 229, 229? And now, I'd like to look at the number 245, 245. Have you found it?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Vojislav Rado Jovanovic, born in 1960 in the village of Tegare and he was killed on the 20th of June 1992, in the village called Tegarska Rieka, is that what it says?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Now could we look on the next page, and the number we are looking for is 317, Milovan Milisav Micic, can you take a look, born in 1957 in the village of Tegare and date of death the 20th of June 1992, in the village called Tegarska Rieka. Is it the person that Riza mentioned to you?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Now, Your Honour, thank you. I would like to -- for the document to stay with the witness because we are going to come back to it. So that will prevent you having to go back and forth all the time with the same papers.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: So in this respect, I'm going to ask you the following question. This part of the village of Tegare which is called Tegarska Rieka, before the war, was it a Serb or a Muslim hamlet? What was the majority population in that part of the village?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: There were three Muslim and -- houses and one Serb house.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Right. This date of death, the 20th of June, is it in line with the time when you noticed something happening around Tegare and when you met Riza?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Let's set this document aside for the time being. I'm going to ask you something else. Mr. Tiro, did you yourself in June and July 1992 engage in any fighting? Were you a fighter?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: For what reason?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: Because I had no weapons, and also I had to provide for my family because they were all dependent on me.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Do you remember the 21st of June 1992? Were you in the area of Ratkovici on that day?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Where were you?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: I was in the nearby forest near my village.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: And now I'm going to put another question to you. You're very familiar with there area of Mocevici. You mentioned that. That was where your family was. Was it possible to enter Ratkovici from the direction of Mocevici?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: For what reason?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: Because there were heavy weapons there. They were there -- front lines there. And there was no access at all.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Right. Do you remember the second half of June 1992, were there any attacks on Mocevici from the area that we are talking about now, from the Serb villages?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: Yes, on a daily basis.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: What were the weapons used?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: They were shelled and other sorts of levy weaponry was used as well as infantry weaponry.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: At the end of June in 1992, did you join any combat in Bradjevina?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Why?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: Because my mother was on her dying bed and I couldn't leave her with my sisters.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Did you hear from anyone, anything about the fight in Bradjevina?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Who did you hear it from?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: By Vekaz Husic. He told me that they could no longer stand the shelling and the attacks.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: What did he tell you what really took place?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: He told me that a group of people assembled with rifles headed by Vekaz Husic, as well as thousands of civilians, and thus Bradjevina was exiled.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: When did you see Bradjevina? To clarify, you said thousands of civilians were there. Could you repeat what you said? It is not clear what happened with Bradjevina?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: Vekaz Husic and several people who had rifles.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: What was the last part you said? Did I correctly understand that they drove the Serbs from Bradjevina?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Because it was unclear in the transcript.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Your Honour, excuse me up to now I think Madam Vidovic has done a fine job of not suggesting or leading with the witness, but I think this last statement was not necessarily something that came directly out of the witness's mouth. So maybe he could just be asked the question "what did he say?" and then we can go from there as to what he meant.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. I my Ms. Sellers is correct, Madam Vidovic. Please. Have you understood her?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. But I understood that the witness would have to go all over again on Bradjevina. I just wanted him to say the last part of his response that was unclear on the transcript.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: What is it precisely that you said?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: That there were thousands of civilians.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Could you please complete the story?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: They drove the Serbs away from Bradjevina.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: That's what I understood you said.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: One moment. Are you satisfied with that, Ms. Sellers?

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: At the beginning of July of 1992, did you see Bradjevina in person?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: Yes. At the beginning of July.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Did you go there?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: I went through Bradjevina.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Were you alone or in someone else's company?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: My brother-in-law and my brother as well.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: I'm asking you about July, not about August of 1992. Did you at the beginning of July of 1992, after your mother passed away, did you see Bradjevina?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Why did you go to Bradjevina then?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: To find food.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: On that occasion, apart from you, were there other people there?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: Thousands of people.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: What were they doing?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: They were taking food, construction material, in order to better their situation because they were living outside.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: You say construction material. What do you have in mind?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: Material, window frames, doors, bricks, anything they could get to provide some sort of shelter for their families.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Was that material taken off or from the houses?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: What you saw in Bradjevina, could you see whether the houses were burned down?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: Not all of them, just two.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: All right. Did you go through the area of Bradjevina at the end of August of 1992?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Can you remember exactly when in August?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: On the 23rd of August of 1992.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Why do you remember that date?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: Because two days after that, my brother-in-law was killed.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: What did you see then, when you passed through Bradjevina?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: We saw that the houses were there still, and that only Stanisa's house and Milo Milanovic's house were torched.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: When you say Stanisa, is that Stanisa Stevanovic?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: I may have misinterpreted your answer. Were those two houses burned down in July? Did you see them in July?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: You mean Stanisa's Stevanovic's and Milan Milanovic's who.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. Were they already burned down?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: No they were burned down later. I saw it when I came there on the 23rd of August.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: That's when you saw that they were burned down? In other words, in July of 1992, they were still standing.

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: They were not torched because the people of Mocevici prevented it.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Did anyone try to prevent the civilians to take the material away from the houses?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: Yes. The people of Mocevici.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Why?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: They offered us to move into the houses.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Did you want to move in?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Why?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: Because that place was shelled on a daily basis because they were following the movement of our civilians.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Who followed your civilians?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: The Serb army.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Did I understand you correctly that Bradjevina could easily be seen from the surrounding area?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: Yes, from almost any village.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: And you said that it was shelled often?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Do you have any knowledge as to where it was shelled from?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: Yes. It was shelled from the side of Ratkovici, Fakovici, from Serbia, by Mackov Kamen called Njemic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: When you say Ratkovici, what part of Ratkovici do you have in mind? I'm not talking about before June 1992, but in the relevant period when there were still Muslim civilians walking through Bradjevina, so that was after the beginning of July. Where was the shelling coming from?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: Ratkovici, Fakovici, Mackov Kamen called Njemic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: From what position in Ratkovici was it possible for one to shell?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: Ratkovici are at a higher altitude than Bradjevina. They see Bradjevina directly.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Were certain areas in Ratkovici in Serb hands then?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. That shelling of Bradjevina, how often did it occur?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: On a daily basis.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Were the shells hitting houses in Bradjevina as well?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Could we please go back to that photograph showing Milenko Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. Stevanovic? This house next to Stevan Stevanovic, can you recognise it?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the photograph be moved slightly on the ELMO so that we could see that part of the house that is in the photograph? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: According to what you know or what you saw or been through in the area where you lived, can you conclude that this is a house from Bradjevina?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: Yes, the old and the new house owned by Stevan Stevanovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Where did the damage come from, in your opinion?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: This was a direct hit by a grenade.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: So you can link that to a grenade or a shell?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: I could also see that the new house or, rather, its roof was hit by a shell.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: So you saw that damage as well?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, you can move the photograph. Perhaps this would be a good time for a break. I apologise. If I may, Ms. Sellers --

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Whose house was this?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: Milenko Stevanovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. In the transcript it was Stevan Stevanovic?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Sellers?

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Your Honour, it's uncertain -- certainly not apparent to the Prosecution at this point that the witness is testifying about the photograph, having recognised the structure, and now talking about the roof on the structure. Is it clear that he's talking about a building that is the same one in this photograph, another building? That does not-- it's not apparent to the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. I think that once this has been raised it can be clarified by the witness.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: And also when, Your Honour, we have a time period --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Madam Vidovic, you put the question to him, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Did you recognise the houses in the photograph?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: I can recognise them in the photograph, and I know what they look like now.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Let us discuss about them. Let's talk about 1992, when you said you went through Bradjevina. Did you see those houses then?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: When you talked about the damage on these houses, did you mention the roof of one of them?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: The one that is behind his back, the new house. I was present when it was hit by a shell in the roof directly.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: When was it?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: The first or the 2nd of July.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: When you went there in July 1992?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I hope it is clear now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. Yes, we can have a 25-minute break starting from now. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Madam Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Tiro, we discussed the shelling of Bradjevina. Could you tell the Chamber whether the Muslims of that area at that time had any grenades in their possession?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Do you have any knowledge as to what happened in Stanatovici at the end of June of 1992?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: What happened there? Did you see anything or hear anything?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: I didn't see it, but I was told by Husic, Vekaz, that the people from Stanatovici withdrew by themselves and they torched their own village in order to prevent the Muslims to acquire some food and other things that they needed.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: I want to change the topic now, Mr. Tiro. In May, June and at the beginning of July of 1992, if I understood you correctly, you spent your time in that area. Did you hear anyone mention the presence of any sort of units from other areas, from Srebrenica itself, in June 1992, in the combat activities that took place in that area?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: You are familiar with the area. Were Mocevici isolated, separated from Srebrenica and other -- were Mocevici, or were they not, separated from Srebrenica and other large Muslim villages?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Sellers?

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Your Honour, it's not apparent to us whether Madam Vidovic is referring to first of all geographically the area of Stanatovici, in terms of hearing about any other units, and whether she is referring -- if we could just clarify, are we still talking about Serb units? Because up until now my impression has been that the witness has been limiting himself to testimony about Serb units.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Madam Vidovic. You only need to explain because you did actually ask the witness -- you spent your time in that area, which area? I mean, you need to be specific, especially since he had referred to Stanatovici immediately before.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: I would ask you the following: Do you still have the map in front of you? Could you please show where Stanatovici are on the map and mark them, please.

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: [Indicates] Where should I show?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Usher, could you go and assist the witness, please?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation].

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: I believe you underscored it already. Just show it to the Chamber.

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: [Indicates] They are here.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: So these are Stanatovici. I was talking about the area of your part of Podrinje, including Mocevici and the surrounding Serb villages. Is that what you understand -- how you understood my question?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: And I asked a couple of questions about Stanatovici and you explained.

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: I want to move on to a different topic and to ask you about Mocevici itself. Are you quite familiar with the area around Mocevici, and the entire area, including Serb and Muslim villages around Ratkovici, Fakovici, Bjelovac and so on and so forth? Are you familiar with the area?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: As regards that, I wanted to ask you the following, and I have in mind June of 1992. In June of 1992, was the village of Mocevici isolated from Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Could you explain the Chamber why you think the village was isolated?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: Because it was surrounded by the Serb villages, as well as all other Muslim villages.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Does that mean that some sort of an army was present there?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: I meant the army of the enemy side.

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: And a lot of it, from all of the villages that were previously marked.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: One moment. I noticed your microphone switched on for a while.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Yes, I'm sorry. I accidentally switched it on. I just wanted to allow the testimony to move on. There was a question of clarity.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, by way of clarification, I asked you about the enemy armed forces as regards the Muslims. You said Mocevici were surrounded by the Serb forces or some other.

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: The Serb forces.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: At that time, and according to what you know, was there any sort of communication in existence between that part of Mocevici and Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Why not?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: Because there were villages in between, the villages of Spat and Pribicevac.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: What was there in Spat and Pribicevac? Please explain to the Chamber?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: Spat was an ethnically pure Serb village, as well as Pribicevac.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Were there any armed forces in Spat?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: Yes, there was, commanded by Sretan, the son of Ilija, but I can't remember the last name.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: All right. And how about Pribicevac?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: They also had an armed presence, and it was completely surrounded by mines.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. After your mother died, what was the situation with the rest of your family? Were you starving?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: Yes, to a large extent. Not only that we didn't have any food but we didn't have any shelter either.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: What did you decide to do?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: When I lost my mother, I spoke with my sisters and brother and my brother-in-law and their two children. We decided to try to break through to Srebrenica under any cost.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: What did you expect to find in Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: At least some sort of shelter or refuge.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: So what did you do then?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: We started from Mocevici, along the road towards Skenderovici but we couldn't enter Skenderovici.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Why, Mr. Tiro?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: Because that village was also under heavy attack by the Serbs, because that was another village that was completely severed from other Muslim villages. So we had to go around through a pine forest that was very dense in order to come out behind Pribicevac.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Did you encounter any difficulties en route?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: Yes, when we got to that pine forest. I don't know whether they had noticed us or not, but there was a great deal of shooting.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: What did you do?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: My son-in-law and myself simply took the kids because we were the strongest, and down there, behind Pribicevac, we simply jumped into a creek and then my brother and my sister did the same, and so nobody was injured at that stage.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: And did you manage to break through to Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: Yes. By way of that creek, and then we got to one end of Srebrenica, not the beginning of the town, but I remember that I went through this creek and we entered the part of Srebrenica called Petrica.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: One moment, I see in the transcript he says my son-in-law. Is that correct? Did he have a son-in-law at the time?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Tiro, did you mention that you had a brother-in-law maybe?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, it was a brother-in-law. My sister got married back in 1983.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: And the time when you entered Srebrenica was after the 4th of July 1992. Did I understand you correctly?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: Yes, on the 6th or the 7th.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you. So this has been cleared up now. How did you find Srebrenica, do you remember?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: When I entered Srebrenica, I almost was sorry for having come, when I saw what had happened to that town.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: What did it look like?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
