utterances.text: It looked horrible, the houses had been burnt, not just a couple but most houses, and I immediately realised that it was impossible for us to find some kind of housing there, for myself and for my family, I mean.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: And did you manage to find accommodation any way? Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: Yes. I was going through Srebrenica and I got to the bus stop, and there across the street I found a smallish house.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: How many of you stayed at this smallish house?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: At that time, my family and myself.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: How many?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: There were 12 of us. And afterwards, some other relatives joined us, and we had to take them in as well, so in three rooms there were 17 people.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: How big were the rooms?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: Three metres by three and a half or three by three.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I'm going to put another question to you now. In the period of time that you were in your village in May and June 1992, did many people go missing on their way to Srebrenica in an attempt to break through and break out of that area and get to Srebrenica? Do you know anything about that?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: I do know of some people who went missing, some people who were killed or who were badly injured. They lost their legs or whatever.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Well, at the period of time when you were in Srebrenica between the 6th and the 7th of July and onwards, did you hear about people going missing from the villages? I mean, people who went from Srebrenica to look for food in those villages?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could I ask the usher to show Defence Exhibit to the witness, it's D589. And it is a list of civilians who went missing from the area of the municipality of Bratunac.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Tiro, whilst we are waiting for you to get this document, I'm going to put another question to you. Does this fact of people going missing refer to the civilians having come from Bratunac as well?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: Yes. They were all civilians at the time.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Fine. Mr. Tiro, I'd like you to take a look at this list. Can you look at page 4 of the document?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, in the English version of the text it's page 6.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: And you, Mr. Tiro, should look at page 4. We've got numbers starting with 1 until 36. Do you know any of the people on the list? It's page 4 for you, sir. Have you managed to find it?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Do you know any of the people here? Look at the bottom part of the text because there are references to Tegare. From number 13 onwards, do you know any of these people?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: Zulfija Zildzic, Amira Alic, Nihada Alic, Ismet Jahic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, these are numbers 30, 31, 32, and 36 in the document.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Could you tell me how come you know these people?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: They are all my neighbours, and Amira Alic is a sister-in-law.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: When was the last time that you saw these people?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: The last time I saw them was at some point in mid-May.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: I would like to ask you whether they stayed behind in the Mocevici area when you left?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: Yes, they left -- they stayed behind.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Right. Did you hear anything about what happened to them?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: They were taken captive. They were in Bratunac, and these three people were released, I know they were released.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Which ones?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: Amira and Nihada Alic and Zulfija Zildzic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Did they tell you about their experiences, about what they went through in Bratunac?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: Amira Alic did say, but her sister, Nihada, she was a child. She was not even seven years old.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: And what did Amira say?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: She said that a Serb would provoke her and took her out of the camp.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Right. Thank you. I would now like you to look at page 8 of the document -- or rather, page 5, and page 8 in the English version. So the next page, basically, is the list of missing persons from Bratunac municipality. Could you take a look at the names of these people? Do you know anyone? It's page number 5 in the Bosnian version. It's a very short list. Just a couple of names. Can you see whether the first name on the list is Hajda Mujic?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Do you know these people?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Who do you know?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: I know all of them.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us about their fates?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: These people went missing when they were looking for food, from Tegare and Orlica.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: You mean looking for food?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: Yes, looking for food.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Could you look at the name Mujanovic, Nazif, does it mean anything to you?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: That was the boy who on the day when his grandparents were killed, on the 12th of May, was taken to an unknown location.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Has he ever come back?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: Never.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Has anyone else come back, any of the people on this list?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Right. We already have an exhibit number for this document. I would just like now to ask you, sir, how you found out about the destiny that befell those people?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: Because --

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: We can continue.

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: Because we went looking for food as well and a neighbour of mine, Ibrahim Mujanovic, told me about that because he was present as well and he managed to get out.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: So he saw them being captured?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Did he tell you who actually captured them?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: He simply told me that it was the Serbs from Orlica and Tegare. He didn't see anyone else from the outside.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: One moment. Judge Eser, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ESER
utterances.text: This is just a question before we leave this document, just a question with regard to language. The witness, if you go back to the list which in the English is on page 6, and I think it was on page 5 in the Serbo-Croat, the witness very often speaks of neighbours. Now, I'm not quite sure what he means with neighbours because all these people are not from list home place but from Tegare. Now, perhaps neighbour in Bosnian, Serbian means something different from English. In English, neighbours, I think, these are people who live around, and it's difficult to understand why he had so many neighbours, even in Tegare. Just to clarify this point.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, could you please explain how far Tegare is from your own house?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: It is only 500 metres away.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Yeah. Only 500 metres. And could you explain to the Trial Chamber what you mean when you say "neighbours"? Who do you mean?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: I mean the villages which are close to my own village, the surrounding villages as well.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, apparently in our language it has a broader meaning than in German.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Same in my language. Let's make a distinction between immediate neighbours and neighbours. That explains it all. Immediate neighbours are those who live in the same street, almost next door to you while others who live nearby can still be your neighbours. So this is -- at least it's clear on I thank Judge Eser and Madam Vidovic and the witness for making it clear for us.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: By the end of August 1992, you said that -- I mean what I understood you to say was that you left in July and that in August 1992, together with other members of your family, including your brother-in-law, you went to live in Srebrenica. Is my understanding correct?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: By the end of August 1992, and generally speaking in August 1992, was your family in a difficult situation in terms of food?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Did you do anything about it?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: Yes, we did. We decided to try and get back to our village, and we set out through the forest.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Why back to your village, precisely?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: Because that's where I was most familiar with the area.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: And you said we decided we should go through the woods. So who decided this together with you?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: I myself, my brother, Mehmed Tiro, and my brother-in-law, Batiti [phoen].

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Was there anyone else there?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: A neighbour called Hamdija Hadzic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Do you know how far you managed to get?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: On that occasion, we travelled a long time. We set out from Srebrenica across the creeks and forests. It took us a long time. All I know is that I got near Mocevici in the morning.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: How long did you stay in that area?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: You mean Mocevici?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: We did not linger. We simply went ahead and went in the direction of our village.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Fine. And how long did you stay in your own village?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: We stayed two days.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: And what happened then? Did you go back to Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: We got to the village, we took some food, and we set out for Srebrenica, in the direction of Grabovica, Ruljevici, and Ivanisovici.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Why in the direction of those villages?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: Because I knew that they had fertile fields, that crops had been sown on that I could find some beans and potatoes and other vegetables there.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: And do you remember how far you managed to get?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: We got as far as Ruljevici. We got to a field which was called Bare, ponds.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Who was the owner of that field?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: It belonged to Petko Prokic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: And what did you do?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: We picked some beans, string beans, and we got some potatoes, and my brother-in-law and I stopped for a cigarette, and then we tied a horse a little fit further to graze.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Could I just ask you what sort of clothes you used to wear, you yourself, your brother, et cetera?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: We wore civilian clothes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Did any one of you have at least a part of any military uniform?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: And can you explain what happened next?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: We didn't manage to smoke a cigarette. I heard a voice behind me and somebody swore at us, and they started shooting straight away.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Did you see that person?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: I just turned around and I could see Stanisa Stevanovic and he was accompanied by some other people, and, at that moment, I jumped over the hedge and I could see that my son-in-law had fallen to the ground and he was screaming.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Again, it's not son-in-law, it has to be brother-in-law.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. It's "zet," which is a brother-in-law. You said that you went over the hedge. Did you feel anything at that stage? Were you injured?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: Whilst I was running away, I could feel something weird in my left arm, and so I hid behind the horse and all the bullets hit the horse, and basically I could run away through a forest and I managed to save my life.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Were you wounded?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: Yes, in my left hand. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Do you have any consequences? Can you show us?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: Yes, of course. My hand -- my arm basically goes stiff whenever the weather changes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Can you show it?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: Yes. It's this finger there.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Tiro, at that stage, did you manage to see what happened to your brother-in-law and your brother? You already said that your brother-in-law was screaming that he was mown down. Did you see in what part of the body he was shot?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: It was just below the knee.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: And did you see what was happening to your brother?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: And what did you hear afterwards, if you heard anything at all?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: When I was already in the woods, I heard a machine-gun being fired.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Did anyone shout anything?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: Stanisa Stevanovic was shouting, "don't run away. You can't run away from us."

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: At what time of day did this happen?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: At 12.00 exactly.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: And what did you do next? Did you manage to take shelter somewhere and what happened next? Can you tell us?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: Yes. That man called Hamdija Hadzic, since he managed to escape as well, we down to the river behind the school in Ruljevici, and there was a kind of valley there around the river and we went and hid behind a wall and we waited until darkness fell.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Did he help you with your wounds or not?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: Yes. He ripped up his shirt and he tied it around the wound so as for me not to bleed to death.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: And what happened then? You said you waited until the night-time. What happened then?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: I wanted to find out what happened to my brother-in-law and my brother, whether they were dead or wounded or perhaps whether they had gone missing altogether.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: So have I understood you correctly, you have just said that you wanted to turn back?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: And did you manage to get back to that place?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: Yes. When darkness fell, together with Hamdija Hadzic, I went back. I couldn't find my brother anywhere and my brother-in-law was lying on the ground. And his left leg had been cut off completely, and there was a bullet wound in his head, and the entire back of his head was missing, his brains were spilling out on to the road.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: What did you do?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: What could I do? I was wounded, and we simply dragged him. The other guy helped me a little bit and he actually tried to tie his head together so that it didn't fall to pieces, and then at the end of the night we got to Mocevici.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: All right. What did you think about your brother's fate at the time?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: I had no hope to see him alive again, because I've either thought he would have been killed.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Did you ever actually find out what happened to your brother?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: Yes. I found out by the end of 1992.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Did you get a message that came with the international convoy that entered Srebrenica? Did they have a message for your family?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: The first convoy that entered Srebrenica, well, that was the happiest day of my life. I heard straight away from my sisters because they were the one who is were reading the letter, and they were really pleased, and they said, well, our brother is alive.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: I understood that you got a letter. Did they bring any other letters?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: Yes, quite a few letters.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: When did you see your brother again?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: I saw him again only as late as 1999.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Did you talk about the event in August 1992 with him? About what happened once you parted your ways?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: Yes. I was really interested.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Tiro, it is extremely important for us to have a break between the question and the answer. So what exactly did he tell you?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: I was extremely interested in it because I was present on that occasion, so the two of us didn't really want to discuss it in front of our sisters or in front of the children of one of the sisters, so we sat apart from anyone else and then I asked him what they did to him, where they took him, whether he was beaten, and he told me his story.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell me what he told you? What happened after you all scattered after the first shots that were fired and when your brother-in-law was shot?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: He was also shot just below the knee, and he was shot in the bone almost but -- and he was also shot in his hand, and his hand is basically paralysed even now, and he was not assisted in any way.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Just take it easy. Did he tell you about your brother-in-law? Did he tell you anything about the brother-in-law?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: Yes, he explained it to me in great detail.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: What did he say?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: He said that Stanisa's colleagues captured him when he was wounded and they dragged him in the direction of the place where the brother-in-law was killed, and Stanisa put the machine-gun against my brother-in-law's head and he blew his brains out.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell me whether he or anyone else said anything to your brother on that occasion? Did your brother tell you?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: The others wanted to kill my brother as well. Stanisa said, "No, I need him alive."

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Did he say why?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: What did he say?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: He said because he wanted to find out who participated in the action at Bradjevina, and who killed Slavko Jovanovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: When you say who participated in the action, do you mean what Muslims or what Serbs?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: What Muslims participated and whether my brother himself participated as well.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Right. And did he tell you what happened next?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: What did he say?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: He said that he was then basically made to board a tractor and then he was taken to the Serb command post at Fakovici.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Did he say anything about being questioned there?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: Yes. He was questioned by Stanisa Stevanovic himself.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Did he say anything about any medical assistance being provided to him?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: What did they do to him?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: He was seriously wounded so he tended to lose consciousness. So they put him in a car, he didn't remember what car it was, and they took him to Skelani, and they took him to prison there.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: And can you tell me about what went on at that prison in Skelani? Was he given medical assistance straight away?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: No. For the first four days, he was given no medical assistance.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: And when was he given some medical assistance, if any?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: On the fifth day, the prison manager could see that his leg was basically lost, and he gave him some cigarettes, and he shouted at his people, and he took him to the hospital at Uzice straight away.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Do you remember his name?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: I don't remember his first name but I do remember his family name. I don't know whether he was a judge or a lawyer. Somebody called Zekic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. If you can -- you've got a few more questions on this, close it.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Just a couple more questions on this topic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Sellers.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Your Honour, prior to Madam Vidovic continuing with this, I would just like to inform the Trial Chamber but also Madam Vidovic that this information concerning the brother and brother-in-law in Skelani, we were just unaware that this was going to be part of the direct-examination, from the summary. If there is any further information you could advise us on it would be quite helpful, possibly prior to tomorrow's continued examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Madam Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I'm going to stand up now because I actually discussed this event and the people involved with the colleagues from the Prosecution, and I insisted on a statement that I know will be in the Prosecutor's office, and I've discussed Stanisa Stevanovic with them on a number of occasions. And I'm really astonished that the Prosecution is claiming that they did not know that we might bring this up and discuss these facts with this witness, because more specifically in fact we discussed a statement that I myself got from the Prosecutor's office. I mean, and apart from anything else, it was only logical to conclude that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Please discuss this among yourselves after the sitting is over, but this has been a very tiring sitting for -- must have been a very tiring sitting for the interpreters trying to catch up. Please finish the next few questions that you have so that we'll give them a rest.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour. I only have two or three questions.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Could I just ask you whether your brother told you what Stanisa Stevanovic asked him about in the course of that questioning that you referred to earlier on?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: He said that he questioned him about who was involved in the attack on Bradjevina, whether he himself participated in that attack and who killed Slavko Jovanovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. Could you tell us how long your brother spent at the hospital in Uzice?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: 28 days.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Could you just tell the Trial Chamber very briefly how he managed to get out of the hospital?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: He got out with the help of a doctor, of a lady doctor who worked at the hospital.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Your brother didn't want us to mention her name?

utterances.speaker: HAMED TIRO
utterances.text: He did not want her name mentioned for her own safety.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours. I think we can stop now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And I think you have most of the information you required, at least out of the evidence, Ms. Sellers. We will continue tomorrow morning at 9.00. In the meantime, I wish to thank the interpreters and technicians for having overstayed a few minutes with us. I realise it must have been difficult for you today. I thank you.
